caption: The drawing depicts a circular plaque located in the center of an off-white, vertically-oriented rectangular background. The plaque itself is rendered in shades of brown and sepia, giving the appearance of wood. Within the circular plaque, there is a detailed relief of an eagle with its wings partially spread, facing to its left (the right side of the image). The eagle is perched on a horizontal object resembling a stick or branch, clutched in its talons. The background of the plaque within the circle is uniformly shaded to emphasize the three-dimensional appearance of the eagle. At the bottom left of the drawing, there is a rectangular label with typewritten text that provides details about the object: it identifies the subject as a plaque made of Spanish cedar, stained and varnished, dating to around 1853, from a privately-owned original, with rendering attributed to Virgil A. Liberto for the Texas Project, Index of American Design, National Gallery of Art. The overall composition is straightforward and centered, with significant negative space surrounding the central image and the label.
title: Plaque
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
